hook: "Don't know how to market your app?"
body: Cesar Alvarez pitches the UGC reaction + app demo format as the ad format for almost any product: start with someone reacting to the app (surprised, emotional, impressed) — it feels authentic, grabs attention, creates curiosity — then show the app in action. Notes the whole pipeline can be done with AI (build the app with Anything, make the marketing with Arcads).
idea: Reaction + demo is the universal app ad format — the reaction earns attention, the demo earns the install.
sequencing: The question hook: don't know how to market your app.
Name the format: UGC-style reaction + app demo.
Beat 1: the reaction — surprised, emotional, impressed; authentic, attention-grabbing, curiosity-creating.
Beat 2: the app in action.
The AI shortcut: build with Anything, market with Arcads, no creators needed.
formatting: X text post, no media.
why_it_works: The reaction is social proof of the demo's payoff — you watch the demo to understand the reaction.
what_to_steal: LC's version: a creator's shocked reaction to the waterproof test, then the demo (shower/pool/sweat test).

hook: "I analyzed 500+ UGC videos across 30 apps. 9 hooks showed up in 80% of the top performers."
body: Lucas Patiri's analysis of 500+ UGC videos across 30 apps: 9 hooks appear in 80% of top performers — (1) POV hook, (2) reaction discovery (highest-converting), (3) 'that friend who...', (4) before/after transformation, (5) guilty confession, (6) pure question hook, (7) surprising stat in the first 0.5s as on-screen text (60%+ hook rates), (8) 'I was doing it wrong' switch story, (9) routine integration. The pattern: none of them feel like ads.
idea: Nine hooks cover 80% of top app UGC — and the only rule that matters is none of them feel like ads.
sequencing: The analysis claim: 500+ videos, 30 apps, 9 hooks in 80% of winners.
POV plus 'that friend who...': make the viewer the main character; self-tagging content.
Reaction discovery: genuine first-time surprise — highest-converting.
Before/after transformation: show the problem, then the result.
Guilty confession: identity-based relatability.
Pure question hook: 'What app did you use for that?'
Surprising stat in the first 0.5s as on-screen text — 60%+ hook rates.
'I was doing it wrong' plus routine integration; the pattern: none of them feel like ads.
formatting: Long numbered X list post.
why_it_works: Each hook is a native TikTok/Reels trope wearing an ad — the format camouflage is the whole game.
what_to_steal: The 'reaction discovery' and 'surprising stat in the first 0.5s' hooks for LC — e.g. 'POV: you shower in your jewelry for the first time.'

hook: "this video got 4.7M views and showcased the whole product in 10 seconds"
body: Carly North breaks down a video that got 4.7M views while showcasing the whole product in about 10 seconds: first clip is a shocked reaction plus hook text (curiosity about what she'll show), straight into a sped-up app demo (viewer stays engaged), with text on screen explaining the steps. Claims any app can do this.
idea: 11 seconds is enough — shocked reaction, sped-up demo, on-screen steps.
sequencing: Beat 1: shocked reaction + hook text — curiosity about what she'll show.
Beat 2: sped-up demo — the viewer stays engaged.
Beat 3: on-screen text explaining the steps.
The claim: any app can do this.
formatting: X text post with a video link.
why_it_works: Speed is the retention hack — the sped-up demo keeps eyes locked, and text steps make it rewatchable.
what_to_steal: LC's 11-second version: shocked reaction to a tarnish-free reveal → sped-up waterproof demo → on-screen text steps.

sequencing: The results: 250K downloads from 2 UGC formats.
Format 1: reaction + app demo.
Format 2: the yap format — 1.3M views, 9K saves, 32K likes.
The yap's hook: extreme and scroll-stopping.
The guide offer: comment 'YAP' for hooks, pacing, and structure.

hook: "If I took over your stuck ad account today, here's the exact order I'd change things to find a winner:"
body: Nick the Riot's stuck-account playbook, in order: (1) new avatar, (2) new creative style — AI UGC, animation, unboxing, reaction, native, (3) new text hook — curiosity-driven, not benefit-driven, (4) new visual hook — film in an uncommon location, (5) new voiceover style, (6) new avatar + new format, (7) new avatar + new hook, (8) same messaging repackaged into 3 formats, (9) same avatar + 3 visual hooks per ad. Launch all of it in a fresh ad set inside the main CBO.
idea: Unstick an account in a fixed order — avatar, style, hook, location, voiceover — before touching the message.
sequencing: New avatar — one never tested.
New creative style: AI UGC, animation, unboxing, reaction, native.
New text hook: curiosity-driven, not benefit-driven.
New visual hook: an uncommon location.
New voiceover style: talking head + B-roll storytelling.
Combos: new avatar + new format, new avatar + new hook.
Same messaging repackaged into 3 formats; same avatar + 3 visual hooks per ad.
Launch protocol: fresh ad set inside the main CBO.
formatting: Numbered X list post.

what_to_steal: LC's stuck-account checklist — reaction sits at #2 on the style list for a reason.
